Question: In a rhombus \(ABCD,\) line segments are drawn within the rhombus, parallel to diagonal \(\overline{BD},\) and terminated in the sides of the rhombus. A graph is drawn showing the length of a segment as a function of its distance from vertex \(A.\) The graph is:

Choices.A: a straight line passing through the origin.
Choices.B: a straight line cutting across the upper right quadrant.
Choices.C: two line segments forming an upright \(V.\)
Choices.D:
two line segments forming an inverted
\(V.\)
